cues.zh: 大家好。

cues.en: I'm here to help you design your life.

cues.en: But I think the most interesting design problem is your life!

cues.en: Well, we teach the class that helps to figure out

cues.en: Now, I'm going to give you the first reframe.

cues.zh: 设计师很喜欢重新定义。
cues.en: Designers love reframes.

cues.en: How many of you hope you never grow up and lose that child-like curiosity

cues.zh: 那份驱动你做每件事的好奇心？
cues.en: that drives everything you do?

cues.zh: 举手看看。对！谁想长大呢？
cues.en: Raise your hand. Right! Who wants to grow up?

cues.zh: 我是说，几乎每场演讲我们都在谈好奇心。
cues.en: I mean, we've been talking about curiosity in almost every one of these talks.

cues.zh: 所以我想把它重新定义为：
cues.en: And so I'd like to reframe this as:

cues.zh: 我们说，我们教的这门课能帮你弄清楚
cues.en: we say we teach the class that helps you figure out

cues.zh: 你接下来想成长为什么样的人，
cues.en: what you want to grow into next,

cues.zh: 随着你的人生、你这精彩的设计徐徐展开。
cues.en: as this life of yours, this amazing design of yours, unfolds.

cues.zh: 所以，设计思维就是我们教的东西
cues.en: So, design thinking is what we teach

cues.zh: 它是一套思维模式，是设计师思考的方式。
cues.en: and it's a set of mindsets, it's how designers think.

cues.zh: 你知道，我们在大学里大概一直被教导
cues.en: You know, we've been taught probably in the university

cues.zh: 要当极度怀疑的实在论者、理性主义者，
cues.en: to be so skeptical realists, rationalists,

cues.zh: 但当你想要做新东西、
cues.en: but that's not very useful as a mindset when you're trying to do something new,

cues.zh: 做前人从未做过的事时，这种思维模式并不太管用。
cues.en: something no one's ever done before.

cues.zh: 所以我说，从好奇心出发，深入你感兴趣的东西。
cues.en: So we say you start with curiosity and you lean into what you're curious about.

cues.zh: 我说，要重新定义问题，因为大多数时候
cues.en: We say you reframe problems because most of the time

cues.zh: 我们发现人们在解决错误的问题
cues.en: we find people are working on the wrong problems

cues.en: and they have a wonderful solution to something that doesn't work anyway.

cues.zh: 那么，在错误的事情上下功夫有什么意义呢？
cues.en: So, what's the point of working on the wrong thing?

cues.en: We say radical collaboration

cues.en: because the answer's out in the world with other people.

cues.zh: 那才是你人生体验所在之处。
cues.en: That's where your experience of your life will be.

cues.zh: 我们要留意自己的过程。
cues.en: We want to be mindful of our process.

cues.en: There are times in the design process when you want lots of ideas,

cues.zh: 也有些时候你真的需要收敛、测试一些东西、
cues.en: and there are times when you really want to converge test some things,

cues.zh: 做一些原型，你要擅长这个。
cues.en: prototype some things, you want to be good at that.

cues.en: And the other is biased action.

cues.en: Now, you know, I'll say that we think

cues.en: no plan for your life will survive first contact with reality.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.en: Reality has the tendency to throw little things at us that we weren't expecting,

cues.zh: 有时是好事，有时是坏事。
cues.en: sometimes good things, sometimes bad.

cues.en: So we say: just have a biased action, try stuff.

cues.en: Why? Why did we start this class?

cues.en: I've been in office hours for a long, long time with my students.

cues.en: I've been teaching here for a while. Dave as well.

cues.en: He was teaching over that community college, in Berkeley, for a while.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.en: And -

cues.en: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, it's a Stanford TEDx.

cues.zh: 但我们注意到，大家经常会卡住、陷入困境。
cues.en: But we notice that people get stuck.

cues.zh: 大家真的会不知所措，不知道该做什么，
cues.en: People really get stuck and then they don't know what to do

cues.zh: 而且似乎没有任何工具能帮自己摆脱困境。
cues.en: and they don't seem to have any tools for getting unstuck.

cues.zh: 设计师也是总会卡住的。
cues.en: Designers get stuck all the time.

cues.zh: 我选择成为一名设计师，
cues.en: I signed up to be a designer,

cues.zh: 这意味着我每天都要面对自己从没做过的东西，
cues.en: which means I'm going to work on something I've never done, every day,

cues.zh: 我会不断地卡住、解脱、再卡住、再解脱。
cues.en: and I get stuck and unstuck, stuck and unstuck, all the time.

cues.zh: 我们也注意到，当我们走出去，不仅和我们的学生交流，
cues.en: We also noticed as we went out and talked to folks who are not just our students,

cues.zh: 还和处于职业生涯中期以及退休后再就业的人们交谈时，
cues.en: but people in mid-career and encore careers,

cues.zh: 发现人们有很多信念
cues.en: that people have a bunch of beliefs

cues.zh: 心理学家称之为“功能失调性信念”，
cues.en: which psychologists label "dysfunctional beliefs,"

cues.zh: 他们相信一些看似真实但实际上并不真实的事情，
cues.en: things they believe that are true that actually aren't true,

cues.zh: 这阻碍了他们。
cues.en: and it holds them back.

cues.zh: 我给你们举三个例子。
cues.en: I'll give you three.

cues.zh: 第一个是：“你的热情是什么？
cues.en: First one is: "What's your passion?

cues.zh: 告诉我你的热情，我就告诉你你需要做什么。”
cues.en: Tell me your passion and I'll tell you what you need to do."

cues.zh: 现在，如果你确实有这样一种热情——
cues.en: Now, if you actually have one of these things, these passions -

cues.zh: 你两岁时就知道你想当医生，
cues.en: you knew at two you wanted to be a doctor,

cues.zh: 你七岁时就知道你想当太阳马戏团的小丑，
cues.en: you knew at seven you wanted to be a clown at Cirque du Soleil,

cues.zh: 而现在你如愿以偿，那太棒了。
cues.en: and now you are one, that's awesome.

cues.en: But we're a sort of research space here at Stanford,

cues.zh: 所以我们去了青少年研究中心，
cues.en: so we went over to the Center for the Study of Adolescence,

cues.zh: 顺便说一下，现在这个中心的研究对象年龄上限已经到了27岁——
cues.en: which by the way now goes up to 27 -

cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.en: He studied this question and it turns out less than 20% of the people

cues.en: have any one single identifiable passion in their lives.

cues.zh: 等你有了，再回来，我们会帮你搞定。”
cues.en: When you have one, come on back and we'll help you with that."

cues.en: So this is not an organizing principle for your search or your design.

cues.en: Don't you know where you're going?

cues.zh: 如果你不知道，那你就晚了。”
cues.en: If you don't know, you're late."

cues.en: I'm not quite sure.

cues.en: But you know, there's a meta-narrative in the culture and when I was growing up:

cues.en: by 25, you're supposed to maybe have a relationship,

cues.zh: 也许已经结婚，开始组建家庭了。
cues.en: maybe have gotten married and started to get the family together.

cues.en: "Oh, that's got to be like 30 or something,"

cues.en: because they can't imagine, anything past, like, 22,

cues.zh: 但30岁离他们还远着呢。
cues.en: but 30 is a long way out.

cues.zh: 但我们知道，现在这些人的人生轨迹灵活得多，

cues.en: Dave and I don't "should" on anybody.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 显然我们都会成为最优秀的。”
cues.en: Obviously we all are going to be the best."

cues.en: Well, this implies that, one, there's a singular best;

cues.en: two, that it's a linear thing, and life is anything but linear;

cues.en: there's an old business saying,

cues.en: "Good is the enemy of better, better is the enemy of best,"

cues.en: and you always want to do your best in business.

cues.en: But if there isn't one singular best, then our reframe is,

cues.en: "The unattainable best is the enemy of all the available betters,

cues.en: because there are many, many versions of you that you could play out,

cues.en: So I'm going to give you three ideas from design thinking -

cues.en: Five ideas from design thinking.

cues.zh: 读过这本书或上过这门课的人
cues.en: And people who've read the book or taken the class

cues.zh: 给我们回信说，
cues.en: have written back to us and said,

cues.en: "Hey, these were the most useful, these were the most doable,

cues.en: they were the most helpful."

cues.en: The number one reason people take our class and we hear read the book

cues.en: is they say, "You know, I want my life to be meaningful,

cues.en: I want it to be purposeful, I want it to add up to something."

cues.en: So, we looked in the positive psychology literature and in the design literature,

cues.zh: 结果发现
cues.en: and it turns out

cues.zh: 有“你是谁”，有“你相信什么”
cues.en: that there's who you are, there's what you believe

cues.en: and there's what you do in the world,

cues.en: and if you can make a connection between these three things,

cues.zh: 如果你能把它变成一个连贯的故事，
cues.en: if you can make that a coherent story,

cues.en: you will experience your life as meaningful.

cues.en: The increase in meaning-making comes from connecting the dots.

cues.en: So we do two things.

cues.en: and they're stuck.

cues.en: They don't like their boss, their partner, their job,

cues.en: there's something that they don't like.

cues.en: But nothing's happening, right? Nothing's happening with them.
